events.title: Java Man
events.description: Fossils of Java Man discovered on Java Island are among the earliest human fossils. These Homo erectus lived approximately 1.8 million to 100,000 years ago, providing important evidence for studying human evolution.

events.title: Srivijaya Empire
events.description: Srivijaya was a powerful maritime commercial empire controlling the Sunda and Malacca Straits, monopolizing sea trade between India and China. Its capital was in present-day Palembang (Sumatra), known for Buddhism.

events.title: Sailendra Dynasty and Borobudur
events.description: The Sailendra Dynasty ruled central Java and built Borobudur, the world's largest Buddhist monument. This magnificent temple represents the pinnacle of Buddhist art and is a World Heritage Site.

events.title: Majapahit Empire Founded
events.description: The Majapahit Empire was established, becoming Java's most powerful Hindu kingdom. Under Prime Minister Gajah Mada's leadership, the empire controlled the entire Indonesian archipelago and parts of the Malay Peninsula.

events.title: Islam Arrives
events.description: Islam was introduced to Indonesia through Arab and Indian Muslim traders. Initially spreading in northern Sumatra, it gradually expanded throughout the archipelago. Islam eventually became Indonesia's dominant religion.

events.title: Dutch East India Company Founded
events.description: The Netherlands established the Dutch East India Company (VOC), beginning to establish colonial footholds in Indonesia. The VOC monopolized spice trade and gradually expanded control over Indonesia.

events.title: Batavia Established
events.description: Dutch East India Company captured Jakarta, renaming it Batavia as VOC headquarters in East Indies. Batavia became center of Dutch colonial rule.

events.title: Java Division
events.description: Mataram Sultanate split into Yogyakarta Sultanate and Surakarta Sunanate. This division resulted from Dutch 'divide and rule' policy, weakening Javanese unity.

events.title: Aceh War
events.description: Dutch waged 30-year war against Aceh Sultanate in northern Sumatra. Acehnese people stubbornly resisted Dutch aggression, making this Holland's bloodiest and costliest colonial war in Indonesia.

events.title: Indonesia Declares Independence
events.description: Two days after Japan's surrender, Sukarno and Hatta proclaimed Indonesian independence, establishing the Republic of Indonesia. August 17 became Indonesia's Independence Day.

events.title: Netherlands Formally Recognizes Independence
events.description: Under international pressure, the Netherlands formally transferred sovereignty to the Republic of the United States of Indonesia. Sukarno became the first president, with Hatta as vice president.

events.title: Bandung Conference
events.description: The Asian-African Conference was held in Bandung with 29 Asian and African countries participating. The conference issued the Bandung Declaration, proposing the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, marking the beginning of the Non-Aligned Movement. Indonesia played an important role on the international stage.

events.title: Anti-Communist Purge
events.description: Under military leadership, Indonesia experienced massive anti-communist violence, with an estimated 500,000 to 1 million killed, mainly communists and ethnic Chinese. This was one of the 20th century's worst mass killings.

events.title: Suharto Comes to Power
events.description: Suharto formally became acting president, then president in 1968, beginning 32 years of 'New Order' rule. Suharto implemented authoritarian governance but promoted economic development.

events.title: Suharto Steps Down
events.description: Under pressure from economic crisis and massive demonstrations, Suharto resigned as president, ending 32 years of rule. Vice President Habibie assumed presidency, and Indonesia entered the Reformasi era.

events.title: Indian Ocean Tsunami
events.description: An Indian Ocean earthquake triggered a tsunami, with Aceh province most severely affected, killing approximately 170,000 people. This was Indonesia's worst natural disaster. Post-disaster reconstruction facilitated the Aceh peace agreement.

events.title: Joko Widodo Elected President
events.description: Former Solo mayor and Jakarta governor Joko Widodo (Jokowi) was elected president. As a president from humble origins, he promised to promote reforms and infrastructure development.

events.title: Asian Games in Jakarta
events.description: Jakarta and Palembang co-hosted the 18th Asian Games. This was Indonesia's second time hosting Asian Games (first was 1962), showcasing Indonesia's development achievements.

events.title: G20 Summit in Bali
events.description: Indonesia served as G20 chair and hosted G20 Leaders Summit in Bali. This enhanced Indonesia's international status and influence.

events.title: Prabowo Elected President
events.description: Former army general Prabowo Subianto won the presidential election and will take office in October. He was Suharto's former son-in-law and Jokowi's former rival, later becoming Defense Minister in Jokowi's government.

events.title: Austronesian Migration
events.description: Austronesian peoples migrated from Taiwan through the Philippines to Indonesian archipelago, bringing agriculture and language. Most modern Indonesians belong to Austronesian language family.

events.title: Early Indianized Kingdoms
events.description: Indian culture spread to Indonesia through trade, forming Indianized kingdoms. Hinduism and Buddhism began spreading in Indonesia, with Sanskrit and Indian art styles influencing local culture.

events.title: Portuguese Conquest of Malacca
events.description: Portugal conquered Malacca, beginning European colonial expansion in Southeast Asia. Portugal sought to control lucrative spice trade.

events.title: VOC Colonial Rule Expansion
events.description: Dutch East India Company (VOC) expanded control over Indonesia, establishing colonial administrative system. VOC monopolized spice and coffee trade, brutally exploiting local population.

events.title: VOC Dissolution
events.description: VOC went bankrupt and dissolved, with Dutch government directly taking over Indonesian colonies. Indonesia became Dutch East Indies colony.

events.title: Java War
events.description: Prince Diponegoro led Javanese resistance against Dutch colonial rule. Though suppressed by Dutch, Java War became symbol of Indonesian nationalism.

events.title: Cultivation System
events.description: Dutch implemented Cultivation System forcing Javanese farmers to grow export crops. System brought huge profits to Netherlands but caused massive Indonesian suffering.

events.title: Budi Utomo Founding
events.description: First Indonesian nationalist organization Budi Utomo established, marking beginning of Indonesian nationalist movement. Organization promoted education and culture.

events.title: Muhammadiyah Founded
events.description: Indonesia's largest Islamic organization Muhammadiyah was established, promoting Islamic reform and modernization. The organization plays important role in Indonesian society and education.

events.title: Indonesian Nationalist Party Founded
events.description: Sukarno founded Indonesian Nationalist Party (PNI), explicitly demanding Indonesian independence. Sukarno became leader of independence movement.

events.title: Japanese Occupation
events.description: Japan occupied Dutch East Indies, ending Dutch colonial rule. Though brutal, Japanese occupation weakened Dutch power, providing opportunity for Indonesian independence.

events.title: Indonesian National Revolution
events.description: Indonesia waged independence war against Netherlands attempting to restore colonial rule. Through diplomatic and military struggle, Indonesia finally achieved full independence.

events.title: Parliamentary Democracy Period
events.description: Indonesia implemented parliamentary democracy but political instability worsened. Frequent cabinet changes, regional rebellions threatened national unity.

events.title: Guided Democracy
events.description: Sukarno implemented 'Guided Democracy', concentrating power. He pursued nationalist and leftist policies, allying with Communist Party, but economy deteriorated.

events.title: West Irian Incorporated into Indonesia
events.description: After years of diplomatic struggle and military confrontation, Netherlands transferred West New Guinea (West Irian) to Indonesia. Indonesian territory was basically determined.

events.title: Asian Financial Crisis
events.description: Asian Financial Crisis severely impacted Indonesia. Rupiah collapsed, economy contracted, millions lost jobs. Crisis triggered anti-Suharto movement.

events.title: First Democratic Elections
events.description: Indonesia held first free democratic elections. Multi-party system established, marking Indonesia's democratic transition.

events.title: East Timor Independence
events.description: After referendum, East Timor separated from Indonesia, becoming independent nation. This ended Indonesia's controversial occupation of East Timor.

events.title: Bali Bombings
events.description: Terrorist bombings in Bali killed 202 people, mostly foreign tourists. This was Indonesia's worst terrorist attack, exposing Islamic extremism threat.

events.title: Aceh Peace Agreement
events.description: Indonesian government signed peace agreement with Aceh separatist movement GAM, ending 30-year conflict. Aceh granted special autonomy.

events.title: Democratic Consolidation
events.description: Indonesia became world's third-largest democracy, successfully holding multiple free elections. Though challenges remain, democratic system gradually stabilized.

events.title: Infrastructure Development
events.description: Jokowi administration prioritized massive infrastructure construction including highways, railways, airports. Infrastructure improvement promoted economic development and national integration.

events.title: New Capital Announcement
events.description: Indonesian government announced plan to move capital from Jakarta to East Kalimantan, building new capital Nusantara. Project aims to relieve Jakarta's overcrowding and develop Eastern Indonesia.

events.title: Economic Challenges
events.description: Indonesia faces middle-income trap challenge, needing economic upgrading and innovation. Corruption, bureaucratic inefficiency remain obstacles to development.

events.title: 普拉博沃當選總統
events.description: 前陸軍將領普拉博沃·蘇比安托在總統選舉中獲勝，將於10月就職。他曾是蘇哈托女婿，也是佐科威的前競爭對手，後來成為佐科威政府的國防部長。...

events.title: 經濟挑戰
events.description: 印尼面臨多重經濟挑戰，包括新冠疫情後復甦緩慢、貧富差距擴大、失業率上升等問題。政府努力推動數位經濟和綠色能源轉型。...
